prompts: Our support assistant's conversations are already saved in Weave. I can't read every exchange. I want it to pick out the ones where the customer sounds confused or annoyed so my team can review them. Where would I set that up, and where would I see the matches? Explain without assuming I know the product's terminology.

output.answer:
**Short answer:** Use a **signal**, which is an automatic scorer that Weave runs on your agent's conversations. You create it and see its matches in the **Signals** tab of the **Agents** view. The preset you want is the **User Frustration** tag.

**Terms**
- **Turn:** one back-and-forth exchange between the user and the agent [S3].
- **Tag:** a label, such as "user-frustration", that a signal attaches to a match [S3].
- **Rating:** a number from 0.0 to 1.0. You don't need ratings for this task [S3].

**Where to set it up**
1. Go to Forge (`https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb`) and select your project [S2].
2. In the sidebar, select **Agents**, which lists the agent conversations saved for the project [S2].
3. In the tab bar, select **Signals** [S2].
4. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer. It offers **Tags** and **Ratings** [S5].
5. Under **Tags**, choose the **User Frustration** preset. The docs say it detects when the user shows signs of frustration, anger, confusion, or dissatisfaction [S6]. That covers both "confused" and "annoyed".

If the presets don't fit, the page also has a **Custom signals** section. I didn't read it, so I can't describe how it works.

**Where you'll see the matches**
The **Signals** tab shows a table of scored turns. Each row is the output of one of your signals [S4]. Useful columns:
- **Scorer:** which signal matched.
- **Last message:** a preview of the last message in that turn.
- **Agent:** which agent the turn belongs to.
- **Scores:** the tag, if matched.
- **When:** when it was scored [S4].

You can narrow the table with the time window selector and the **Filter** bar. You can filter by scorer, agent, score range, or time period [S4]. For example, filter to the User Frustration scorer to build your team's review list.

**Caveats**
- The table only shows rows that matched at least one tag. A tag signal can run successfully and still show nothing [S5].
- If you expect matches and see none, open **Traces** in the project sidebar. Check the scorer name and the **Status** column. Scorer errors show a red indicator with details [S7].
- You can turn signals on or off, edit them, or delete them from the active-signals button in the toolbar [S8].
- The pages I read don't say whether a new signal scores conversations that were saved before you created it. I couldn't confirm that, so create the signal and check whether older conversations show up.
- The docs also say this workflow is available in CoreWeave Agent Lens, using the same trace data [S1].

**Next step:** create the **User Frustration** tag signal, then open the **Signals** tab and filter by that scorer.

sources.text:
## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

sources.text:
#### Tags presets

| Template | What it detects |
| - | - |
| **User Frustration** | User shows signs of frustration, anger, confusion, or dissatisfaction. |
| **Malicious Intent (Jailbreaking)** | User attempts to jailbreak the system, extract restricted content, perform prompt injection, use role-play exploits, or otherwise manipulate the agent into ignoring its guardrails. |
| **NSFW** | User input or agent output contains explicit sexual content, graphic violence, or other material inappropriate for a workplace setting. |
| **Low Quality Response** | Agent output that is factually wrong, off-topic, evasive, repetitive, lacks justification when refusing, or otherwise fails to address the user's request. |

sources.heading: Signals table
sources.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

| **NSFW** | User input or agent output contains explicit sexual content, graphic violence, or other material inappropriate for a workplace setting. |
| **Low Quality Response** | Agent output that is factually wrong, off-topic, evasive, repetitive, lacks justification when refusing, or otherwise fails to address the user's request. |

results.title: Monitor using built-in signals
results.heading: How signals work
results.snippet:
### How signals work

Each signal uses an LLM-as-a-judge approach to classify traces:

* **Trace selection**: Quality signals evaluate successful root-level traces. Error signals evaluate failed traces. Weave doesn't score child spans and intermediate Calls.
* **Prompt construction**: Weave constructs a prompt that includes the trace metadata, inputs, outputs, exception details (if any), and the operation's source code. Weave appends the signal's classifier prompt with instructions for the specific issue to detect.
* **LLM scoring**: For each signal, a Serverless Inference model performs a binary classification (whether that issue is present on the trace). Detected issues are returned as comma-delimited string tags (for example, `"Low-quality, User-frustration, Forgetful"`).

When multiple signals from the same group (Quality or Error) are active, Weave batches the signals into a single LLM call. The model evaluates all active classifiers in one pass and returns a result for each.

```python theme={"system"}
search_agents(
    query: 'str' = '',
    agent_name: 'str | None' = None,
    conversation_id: 'str | None' = None,
    trace_id: 'str | None' = None,
    limit: 'int' = 20,
    offset: 'int' = 0
```

Search agent messages by content, grouped by conversation.

Searches message content (and/or the structured filters below) and returns matching conversations with their matched messages. An empty `query` turns this into structured retrieval over the filters.

* **`query`**: Substring to match in message content. Empty matches all.

* **`conversation_id`**: Restrict to a single conversation.

* **`limit`**: Maximum number of matching messages to consider.
* **`offset`**: Number of matches to skip (for pagination).

results.heading: Shape spans for the Agents view
results.snippet:
## Shape spans for the Agents view

Weave accepts any OTel span and stores all of its attributes, but the Agents view renders spans that follow the [OTel GenAI semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md). Set `gen_ai.operation.name` on each span to tell Weave what the span represents:

| `gen_ai.operation.name` | Represents | Rendered as |
| - | - | - |
| `invoke_agent` | One complete user-agent exchange. | A turn. |
| `chat` | One call to a language model API. | An LLM call within a turn. |
| `execute_tool` | One tool execution. | A tool call. |

* `gen_ai.conversation.id`: Groups turns into a conversation. Use a stable ID for the lifetime of the conversation.

# Review items in an annotation queue

> Evaluate trace items and submit structured feedback using a simplified review interface.

Annotation queues provide a focused review interface for domain experts. You review one item at a time, examine the provided context, and submit structured feedback using predefined fields. By completing a queue, you contribute expert judgments that your team can use to evaluate and improve LLM outputs.

You don't need to understand the underlying model or tracing system to complete reviews. This lets external experts review the data without needing broader project context.

result.heading: Signals table
result.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

The drawer groups available signals into two categories:

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. * **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

## Create a new signal

To start scoring your agent's turns, create one or more signals. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer.

sources.heading: Signals table
sources.text:
## Signals table

The Signals tab displays a table of scored turns from your agent. Each row represents the output of one of your signal monitors. The following columns appear by default.

| Column | Description |
| - | - |
| **Type** | The part of the conversation that gets scored. Only `turn` is supported. |
| **Scorer** | The name of the signal that produced this score. |
| **Last message** | A preview of the last message in the scored turn, with the role shown below. |
| **Agent** | The agent associated with the scored turn. |
| **Scores** | The numeric rating from 0.0 to 1.0, or a tag if matched. We recommend using consistent ratings where 1 indicates good and 0 indicates bad, but your scorers can use any scale you define. |
| **Trend** | Displays an inline chart that shows how this signal trends over time. Shows either the average value (for ratings) or the count (for tags). |
| **When** | When the signal was scored. |

Use the time window selector and **Filter** bar to narrow results by scorer, agent, score range, or time period. The **Score volume** timeline shows counts of signals that Weave evaluated for ratings or tagged. It reflects the rows shown in the table and supports drag-to-filter on the timeline.

results.title: Monitor using built-in signals
results.heading: How signals work
results.snippet:
### How signals work

Each signal uses an LLM-as-a-judge approach to classify traces:

* **Trace selection**: Quality signals evaluate successful root-level traces. Error signals evaluate failed traces. Weave doesn't score child spans and intermediate Calls.
* **Prompt construction**: Weave constructs a prompt that includes the trace metadata, inputs, outputs, exception details (if any), and the operation's source code. Weave appends the signal's classifier prompt with instructions for the specific issue to detect.
* **LLM scoring**: For each signal, a Serverless Inference model performs a binary classification (whether that issue is present on the trace). Detected issues are returned as comma-delimited string tags (for example, `"Low-quality, User-frustration, Forgetful"`).

When multiple signals from the same group (Quality or Error) are active, Weave batches the signals into a single LLM call. The model evaluates all active classifiers in one pass and returns a result for each.

* **Tags**: Apply a label automatically to matching spans, such as `user-frustration` or `nsfw`. Use tags to categorize spans or flag unwanted behavior. The signals UI only displays rows for spans that matched at least one tag, so a tag signal might run successfully even if you don't see any output.
* **Ratings**: Assign a score from 0 to 1 to matching spans. Use ratings to rate agent performance and measure improvements over time.

input.answer:
**Short answer:** Use a **signal**, which is an automatic scorer that Weave runs on your agent's conversations. You create it and see its matches in the **Signals** tab of the **Agents** view. The preset you want is the **User Frustration** tag.

**Terms**
- **Turn:** one back-and-forth exchange between the user and the agent [S3].
- **Tag:** a label, such as "user-frustration", that a signal attaches to a match [S3].
- **Rating:** a number from 0.0 to 1.0. You don't need ratings for this task [S3].

**Where to set it up**
1. Go to Forge (`https://forge.coreweave.com/wandb`) and select your project [S2].
2. In the sidebar, select **Agents**, which lists the agent conversations saved for the project [S2].
3. In the tab bar, select **Signals** [S2].
4. Select **+ New signal** to open the **Create signals** drawer. It offers **Tags** and **Ratings** [S5].
5. Under **Tags**, choose the **User Frustration** preset. The docs say it detects when the user shows signs of frustration, anger, confusion, or dissatisfaction [S6]. That covers both "confused" and "annoyed".

If the presets don't fit, the page also has a **Custom signals** section. I didn't read it, so I can't describe how it works.

**Where you'll see the matches**
The **Signals** tab shows a table of scored turns. Each row is the output of one of your signals [S4]. Useful columns:
- **Scorer:** which signal matched.
- **Last message:** a preview of the last message in that turn.
- **Agent:** which agent the turn belongs to.
- **Scores:** the tag, if matched.
- **When:** when it was scored [S4].

You can narrow the table with the time window selector and the **Filter** bar. You can filter by scorer, agent, score range, or time period [S4]. For example, filter to the User Frustration scorer to build your team's review list.

**Caveats**
- The table only shows rows that matched at least one tag. A tag signal can run successfully and still show nothing [S5].
- If you expect matches and see none, open **Traces** in the project sidebar. Check the scorer name and the **Status** column. Scorer errors show a red indicator with details [S7].
- You can turn signals on or off, edit them, or delete them from the active-signals button in the toolbar [S8].
- The pages I read don't say whether a new signal scores conversations that were saved before you created it. I couldn't confirm that, so create the signal and check whether older conversations show up.
- The docs also say this workflow is available in CoreWeave Agent Lens, using the same trace data [S1].

**Next step:** create the **User Frustration** tag signal, then open the **Signals** tab and filter by that scorer.
